mustKnow.title: Negotiators ‘braced for worst’ over US-Iran talks to reopen strait of Hormuz
mustKnow.snippet: Qatar-mediated talks seek release of over $6bn in Iranian assets in exchange for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, with Gulf states awaiting a US reply.
mustKnow.brief: Gulf officials say they are bracing for the worst while Washington considers an Iranian proposal to reopen the strait of Hormuz. Qatar is mediating indirect talks in Doha over the release of more than $6bn in frozen Iranian assets, and Iran has agreed to shorten a sanctions-and-reopening timetable from seven days to two. The outcome matters because the strait is a key shipping route, and the US midterm elections are on Tuesday.
mustKnow.why: Oil flows and Gulf stability hinge on Washington's reply over frozen assets

mustKnow.title: Ukraine defies Trump to resume attacks on Russian oil refineries
mustKnow.snippet: Ukraine resumed strikes on Russian refineries despite US pressure, with reported fires at the Kstovo and Samara sites just before the midterms.
mustKnow.brief: Russian state media said Ukrainian long-range drones set fire to the Kstovo refinery in Nizhny Novgorod overnight, following a major strike on a Rosneft refinery in Samara oblast. The Kremlin says Kyiv is simply ignoring US wishes, which were reportedly to pause refinery strikes, though Ukrainian officials say they never agreed to a 30-day pause. Zelenskyy has not acknowledged the refinery attacks, and trilateral talks involving Russia, Ukraine and the US are expected later this month.

mustKnow.title: US approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
mustKnow.snippet: The approval covers 500 interceptors for Ukraine's air defence, a major US military commitment to Kyiv against Russian ballistic missile attacks.
mustKnow.brief: The United States has approved a $2.1bn sale of 500 advanced PAC-3 Patriot interceptor missiles to Ukraine, with the cost funded entirely by Kyiv's European allies and Canada. President Zelensky warned that deliveries could take several years, as there is a global shortage of the missiles and new builds are being ordered rather than existing stock. Kyiv says it needs them urgently to counter Russian ballistic missile strikes on the power grid.
mustKnow.why: Biggest air-defence boost yet against Russian ballistic missile barrages

cleantech.title: The electricity system on trial: CFE wants to turn large private consumers into clients
cleantech.originalTitle: El sistema eléctrico, a prueba: la CFE quiere convertir en clientes a los grandes consumidores privados
cleantech.snippet: Large private self-supply users can keep their rates for two years or move to the wholesale market with a government incentive.
cleantech.brief: Under the new scheme, companies with self-supply contracts could keep their current rates for two years. Alternatively, they can move to the wholesale market and receive a government incentive to do so. The move is part of a wider debate over the electricity system, with CFE aiming to win over big private users as customers.
cleantech.why: CFE pushes self-supply users toward wholesale market, reshaping Mexican power deals

cleantech.title: Judge allows NAACP lawsuit over xAI data center pollution to move forward
cleantech.snippet: A court ruling lets NAACP's Clean Air Act claims against xAI's data centre pollution proceed, a relevant precedent for data-centre emissions.
cleantech.brief: A federal judge denied xAI's motion to dismiss a lawsuit by the NAACP, filed through the Southern Environmental Law Center, which accuses the SpaceX-owned company of running at least 35 combustion turbines at its Colossus data center near Memphis without required Clean Air Act permits. xAI had argued the turbines were exempt as mobile sources and that the plaintiffs lacked standing, but the judge ruled the claims can proceed. The case will continue, and a similar Department of Justice motion was also rejected earlier this month.
cleantech.why: Clean Air Act precedent for on-site gas turbines powering data centres

cleantech.title: Will Josh Shapiro’s Data Center Past Haunt his Political Future?
cleantech.snippet: Shapiro reversed course on fast-track permitting for hyperscale data centers, pulling them from the program within about 20 months.
cleantech.brief: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro has faced intense pressure over data centers during the past two years. He first introduced a fast-track permitting process designed to speed up hyper-scale data center projects, then later removed those facilities from the program. The shift raises questions about how the issue could shape his political future.
cleantech.why: Fast-track permitting reversal signals political limits on data-centre load growth

cleantech.title: National Grid to site biggest substation on Teesside, near planned AI datacentre
cleantech.snippet: National Grid is buying 73 acres at Teesside to build a large substation that could power a planned AI datacentre.
cleantech.brief: National Grid has agreed to buy 29.5 hectares of land at Dorman Point on Teesworks, a site earmarked for Britain's biggest electricity substation. The substation could supply up to 3.2GW of capacity to a planned AI datacentre nearby, which Tees Valley mayor Ben Houchen says would help the region compete for investment. The project comes as datacentres face strong public opposition across the UK.
cleantech.why: Grid build-out following AI load in UK's Teesside industrial cluster

ai.title: These firms you've never heard of are feeding fears the AI bubble could burst
ai.snippet: Data centres carry debt running to tens of billions of pounds, raising financing risk concerns behind the AI boom.
ai.brief: Neocloud firms such as CoreWeave and Nebius rent out data centre computers to major AI developers, and their shares have recently fallen sharply. CoreWeave alone has accumulated $35.1bn in debt, and its stock has lost about a quarter of its value over the past month. Analysts warn that the sector depends heavily on big tech spending and on continued cheap borrowing, which makes many firms vulnerable if AI spending slows.
ai.why: Debt-fuelled data-centre builders are the weak link in AI financing

ai.title: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts
ai.snippet: An attack chain using a MathLive library in ChatGPT's sandboxed HTML previews could reach OpenAI APIs and private data.
ai.brief: Parameter Labs disclosed an exploit chain against ChatGPT's HTML preview feature, which renders interactive apps in a sandboxed iframe. By abusing a MathLive virtual keyboard message handler that used innerHTML, and a YouTube oEmbed endpoint allowed by the content security policy, an attacker could run JavaScript inside ChatGPT. A malicious share link could then pull private data from a signed-in visitor's account. OpenAI fixed the flaw and paid a $5,000 bug bounty.
ai.why: Real exploit chain in ChatGPT sandbox; lessons for anyone building agents

ai.title: How a small Wisconsin city scuttled a secretive $1.6bn datacenter project
ai.snippet: Residents and a newly elected councilwoman organised opposition that led the city to reject a $1.6bn hyperscale AI datacentre campus.
ai.brief: Residents of Menomonie, Wisconsin, a city of about 17,000, pushed back against a $1.6bn AI datacenter campus after city officials had quietly signed nondisclosure agreements with the developer, Balloonist LLC, for more than a year. The project would sit on 320 acres and use an estimated 75,000 gallons of water daily, and councilmembers said they received few details before voting to move forward. Public anger grew after residents learned of the plan in July 2025, and the project was ultimately stopped by community opposition.
ai.why: Local opposition now able to kill billion-dollar AI compute projects

world.title: Democrat Haley Stevens endorses Abdul El-Sayed’s Republican rival Mike Rogers
world.snippet: Stevens endorsed Mike Rogers in a video after an event with him in Detroit, an unusual rebuke of her party's nominee.
world.brief: Michigan Democratic Congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the party's Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, endorsed his Republican rival Mike Rogers in a video posted to X after appearing with Rogers at a Detroit church. The move follows a feud over Israel, after El-Sayed refused to disavow an outside group's ad blaming US support for Israel for rising living costs. Michigan's Senate seat could be decisive for Democratic control of the chamber.
world.why: Rare cross-party endorsement could swing a Senate-control race in Michigan
